notes.note: A heatwave summer gave very ripe, concentrated grapes. The berries shrivelled cleanly, so many Mosel, Saar and Ruwer estates made rare Beerenauslese and Trockenbeerenauslese. Heavy, rich, intense wines.
A tiny crop, 30–50 % below normal (about 40 hL/ha at Prädikat estates), with very high acidity. Many estates deacidified. The low yields gave dense wines.

A very hot, dry summer kept mildew away almost entirely. September rain came without rot thanks to cool nights and swelled a large crop. Mosel Riesling averaged about 85 °Oe; rich aromas, moderate acidity.
Cool and wet; downy mildew was hard to control on waterlogged soils. South-facing top sites did best: they reached about 95 °Oe while most of the harvest came in at 70–90 °Oe.
The heatwave vintage brought a historically early harvest. Rich, opulent wines.
Frost on the nights of 26–27 April, the worst in the Côte d'Or since 1985, and unlike 1985 it reached the higher slopes too. Heavy losses: one famous Gevrey domaine lost two-thirds of its crop.

Temperatures plunged on 5 April, then three nights of hard frost from 6 to 9 April. Côte de Beaune whites were hit hardest, with losses around 80 % reported: France's worst agricultural frost since at least 1947.

Rain into mid-June delayed bloom and disrupted fruit set (shatter in places), then a long, cool season and a late harvest with autumn storms. Yields 10–75 % below normal; elegant wines at lower alcohol, a Bordeaux-like Napa vintage.
The South Napa earthquake (M6.0) struck at 3:20 a.m. on 24 August 2014. Stacked barrels toppled in many wineries; an estimated 5,000–6,000 barrels of wine were lost.
A warm to hot season with extreme heat around Labor Day pushed picking early. Most of the crop was in when the wildfires broke out on 8 October; later lots were watched for smoke taint.
The Glass Fire burned more than 67,000 acres and destroyed 1,555 structures in Napa County before it was contained on 20 October. Smoke taint defined late-picked fruit.
A Labor Day heat wave brought five days of triple-digit heat in early September, then mid-September rain. Many varieties ripened at once, compressing the harvest; strict selection was needed.
